title: Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro vs. Logitech G915 X: The Ultimate Mechanical Keyboard Showdown
subtitle: Comparing the best from Razer and Logitech to see which flagship keyboard belongs on your desk in 2025.
author: Technova Team
content:
Choosing a flagship mechanical keyboard in 2025 has become a battle of philosophies. On one side, we have the Logitech G915 X Lightspeed, the successor to a legend, emphasizing low-profile elegance and wireless freedom. On the other, the Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro, a maximalist wired powerhouse designed to be the ultimate command center for your battlestation.

Design and Build Quality

The Logitech G915 X continues the legacy of its predecessor with an ultra-slim aesthetic. It features a premium aluminum top plate and a remarkably thin chassis that looks at home in both a professional office and a high-end gaming setup. The low-profile design isn't just for looks; it offers a more ergonomic typing angle for many users without needing a wrist rest.

In contrast, the Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro is unapologetically large. It’s a full-height keyboard with a robust build, featuring a plush, magnetic leatherette wrist rest that is arguably the most comfortable in the industry. Razer also adds a massive amount of flair with 3-side underglow RGB lighting that spills onto your desk, creating an immersive atmosphere that the slimmer Logitech simply can't match.

Switches and Typing Experience

The G915 X utilizes Logitech's updated GL Low-Profile switches. These have been refined for better stability and a more satisfying bottom-out feel compared to the original G915. They are available in Linear, Tactile, and Clicky variants, all featuring double-shot PBT keycaps for long-term durability.

Razer sticks to its tried-and-true full-height Mechanical Switches (Green for clicky, Yellow for linear). The V4 Pro is built for speed and precision, featuring an incredible 8,000Hz polling rate. While most users won't notice the difference between 1ms and 0.125ms latency, competitive gamers seeking every possible advantage will appreciate the responsiveness of the BlackWidow.

Features and Customization

This is where the two keyboards diverge most significantly. The Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro is a macro-lover's dream. It features the Razer Command Dial, a highly customizable wheel that can control everything from brush sizes in Photoshop to zoom levels in games. It also boasts 8 dedicated macro keys (5 on the side, 3 on the edge), giving you unparalleled control over your workflow.

The Logitech G915 X focuses on connectivity and streamlined control. It features dedicated G-keys and media controls, but its real strength is the Lightspeed Wireless technology. It offers a flawless, lag-free connection that is indistinguishable from a wire, with the added benefit of Bluetooth for multi-device pairing. The battery life has also seen a massive jump, lasting up to 800 hours with the lighting turned off.

The battle between low-profile wireless and full-height wired flagships.

Comparison Table

Feature Logitech G915 X Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro
Profile Low-Profile Full-Height
Connectivity Wireless (Lightspeed), BT, Wired Wired (8K Polling)
Switches GL Low-Profile (PBT) Razer Mechanical (ABS/PBT)
Extra Controls 9 G-Keys, Media Keys Command Dial, 8 Macro Keys
Wrist Rest None Plush Magnetic Leatherette

Final Verdict

The choice between these two comes down to your desk setup and priorities. If you value a clean, wireless aesthetic and prefer the ergonomics of a low-profile board, the Logitech G915 X is the clear winner. It is the most refined wireless keyboard on the market today.

However, if you want a keyboard that acts as a secondary controller for your PC, with endless macro possibilities and the best RGB lighting in the business, the Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro is hard to beat. It is a powerhouse that justifies its desk real estate with pure utility.
